players.product: Server liquid cooling via subsidiary Readore (acquired January 2026): UQD/MQD quick disconnects, inner and rack manifolds, server liquid cooling plates (GB200/GB300) and optical-module cold plates, phase-change liquid-cooling modules, server VC / 3DVC, busbars

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record, H1 2026 results briefing): the RMB's one-way appreciation against the US dollar hurt the company in two ways - overseas business is settled mainly in US dollars, so the same foreign-currency revenue shrank when translated into RMB, and the swings produced large exchange losses that raised finance expenses and markedly weighed on reported profit; in the period exchange-rate moves had a negative effect on both net profit and revenue. The company uses FX hedging and exposure management to limit the impact but said that in extreme cases these may not fully achieve the expected hedging effect; its other response is to keep raising the share of high-value-added business and to build out local overseas supply chains.

Lingyi iTech.why: Its subsidiary Readore makes server liquid-cooling hardware (cold plates, UQD quick disconnects, manifolds) delivered in volume to AI-compute customers and server contract manufacturers, so AI server liquid-cooling build-outs drive its thermal revenue.
Lingyi iTech.evidence: 2026 Half-Year Report: Readore's main business includes server liquid-cooling quick disconnects (UQD), liquid-cooling manifolds, single-phase liquid-cooling modules (server liquid cooling plates and optical-module cold plates) ... as a core supplier to a North American AI-compute leader, it delivers server liquid-cooling and power products in volume to leading overseas AI-compute companies, their supply-chain partners, server contract manufacturers and power-solution companies.
